rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: When a landlord serves a notice to quit or declines to renew a lease, they must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time. They must also send a copy of the notice to quit or non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the city's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.quoted_span: The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.
rules.effective_date_note: FAQ states HSNA becomes effective November 6, 2020; ordinance passed October 2020.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with notice to quit; copy to Office of Housing Stability
rules.penalty: Warning for 1st offense; $300 per day for 2nd and subsequent offenses (enforced by ISD). Violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities. Requirements cannot be waived.

unverifiable_exemptions: residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities
non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities

parsed.doc_summary: Boston FAQ on the Housing Stability Notification Act (Boston City Code § 10-11.7, effective 2020-11-06). It requires a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with any notice to quit or non-renewal, and a copy sent to the Office of Housing Stability. It is a notice rule, not a just-cause limit.
